# Speccify 0.11.0

Speccify 0.11.0 brings named screens, unique resource tabs, structured models
and explicit controls for local and remote work.

## Organize your workspace

- Create more than two named screens. Each resource or resource type has one
  tab across your screens; the complete resource and its type tabs can coexist.
  Existing A/B layouts are preserved.
- Give resource types their own names and icons. Specs, Skills, UseCases,
  Rules, Versions and the new Agents resource share consistent navigation.
- Open the File Editor from **Window → File Editor** or the **</>** button on
  the right of the toolbar. Existing files and drafts remain in their editor.
- Keep your preferred inspector section when changing resources, and copy
  direct links to resources and individual items.

## Model behavior and coordinate work

- Structure systems, workflows and use cases, with actor and UI references.
  Edit up to three levels inline using the same drafts as document tabs.
  Existing UseCase identities and history remain compatible.
- Manage named agent personas, Spec-bound sessions, background work and
  sequential Board flows. Starts, permissions and human decisions remain explicit.
- Inspect activity and duration records, time charts and measured projections.
  Configure scoped data access and controlled delegation without silently
  switching providers or sharing credentials.
- Preview skills from selected Git repositories, compare updates with local
  changes, and develop reusable methods from related completed Specs.

## Voice and local connections

- Dictate into an explicitly selected terminal and review the text before
  sending. Resolve navigation commands to visible targets; speech does not
  grant approval to run an action.
- Pair Macs on a local network for session control, with device authorization,
  controlled input ownership and reconnect handling.

## Share project versions

Version planning can now travel with the shared Spec register, independently
of each collaborator's code branch. Update all participating clients first,
then use **Preview sharing project data…** in the Versions/UseCases overview
and confirm the reviewed change. Existing local data is retained. A colleague
with differing local data can review it and choose **Use shared data and keep
local copy**; the app does not silently merge competing histories.

## Update or install

Use **Environment → Updates** in Speccify, or the
[download page](https://speccify.io/download/). The supported new packages are
**Mac Apple Silicon** and **Windows x64**. Each contains the private Python
runtime and offline dependencies; an existing Python installation is left alone.

The Mac application and DMG are Developer ID signed, notarized and stapled.
Both platforms have verified updater signatures. The Windows installer does
not have an Authenticode signature, so Windows may show an unknown-publisher
warning. New Linux packages are discontinued; older release assets remain available.

## Verification and scope

The exact candidate completed all **121 Mac** and **108 Windows** local check
steps. On a separate Windows x64 machine, the exact installer passed fresh
installation, first start with its app/runtime network access blocked, real
native interaction and an upgrade from 0.10.0 with retained state.

The iOS work in this version supplies a host protocol and executable test
client, not a published iOS app. Hollerpad integration and future Pro/Max
capabilities are preparation work; there is no new paywall. Remote control is
limited to the local network. Source-sharing, model migrations and automation
require their own explicit choices.

Release packages are built and tested on owned Mac and Windows machines.
GitHub hosts source and downloads; the desktop release no longer uses hosted
Actions builds. A native product tour is prepared from the release candidate.
